newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Philippine bourse proposes removal of IPO tax.
newsitem.headline: Philippine bourse proposes removal of IPO tax.

text.p: The Philippine Stock Exchange had proposed the scrapping of a tax on initial public offerings in order to encourage more firms to go public, papers obtained from the Department of Finance showed on Thursday.
It also asked for the abolition of the documentary stamp tax of 1.50 pesos on stock transactions.

It also requested the government to maintain the tax exemption on dividends, saying it would pose a threat to the development of the country's equities market. The government had proposed this as part of its tax reforms package.
Currently a tax of one to four percent is slapped on gross proceeds of the IPO depending on the size of the offering.
"With the imposition of an IPO tax, the attractiveness of equity financing is further diminished vis-a-vis debt financing as a source for corporate financing," the exchange said.
"In fact, nearly 80 percent of corporate funding is obtained through short-term bank loans which has resulted in a highly leveraged corporate sector," it said.
